i^^Y^ annual convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, held in its 128th year
with the Epsilon Phi Chapter, McGill University, as host, was called to order at
9:15 a.m. in the Brittany Room of the Sheraton-Mt. Royal Hotel by R. Lyman
Williams, Epsilon Phi '26, general chairman of the convention. Brother Williams
extended the greetings of the Epsilon Phi Chapter and of its alumni to the
convention.
Brother Williams appointed temporary officers of the convention as follows:
Temporary Chairman Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21
Temporary Recorder Jerome W. Brush, Jr., Delta Delta '39
Temporary Assistant Recorder David A. Binmore, Epsilon Phi '63
Temporary Assistant Recorder Nicholas L. D. Firth, Epsilon Phi '63

Frederick K. Ostermann, Phi '62

A motion was duly adopted that the convention recess briefly to enable the
committees to prepare their reports.
At the end of the recess the temporary chairman called the convention to
order.
John C. Farr, Xi '62, chairman of the Committee on Credentials, announced
preliminary registration of delegates: 27 chapters present with credentials; 3
chapters, the Chi, the Tau and the Theta Epsilon Chapters, absent. The com
mittee reported it would render reports to the convention from time to time as
credentials were presented to the committee. No action was taken by the conven
tion on this announcement.

officers of the convention:
President Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21

2nd Vice President George L. Brain, lota '20

temporary recorder be instructed to cast one ballot for the election of the perma

cast and that the permanent officers had been elected.

organized, to order.
He appointed as parliamentarians for this convention, Edward T. Richards,
Sigma '27, and George L. Brain, lota '20, members of the Executive Council.
A motion was duly adopted, approving the RECORDS of the 1960 Convention
and waiving the reading thereof.
The president called for the reading of the Convention Rules. On motion
duly adopted, the Convention Rules were approved (see Appendix A, page 14).
Recorder Brush called the roll of the chapters and reported that 27 chapters
were represented by delegates and that a quorum was present.

Burton called for a report by the Committee to Nominate Members of the Execu
tive Council. John Graebner, Mu '63, chairman, presented the report of the com
mittee, nominating the following brothers to serve on the Executive Council for
the term expiring with the convention in 1966:
John F. Bush, Jr., Upsilon '22
Robert W. Parsons, Xi '22
Richard M. Ross, Lambda '20
A motion was adopted that this report be unanimously accepted and that the
recorder be instructed to cast one ballot for the election of the brothers nominated.
The recorder reported that the ballot had been cast and that those nominated had
been elected.
The president called for the report of the Committee on Annual Communica
tions and Unfinished Business. Robert L. Joss, Theta Theta '62, chairman, pre
sented the following resolutions:
RESOLVED: That the Annual Communication of the Executive Council
to the 1961 convention be accepted as submitted, with thanks to the committee.
RESOLVED: That the convention approve the payment of 1500 to the
Epsilon Phi Chapter as a contribution toward the expense of running the
convention.
RESOLVED: That the convention authorize the treasurer to transfer
$4,500 of the Diamond Life Subscription Fund to cover the existing deficit
in the Diamond Life Current Fund.
RESOLVED: That an allotment of 50^ per undergraduate member of
the fraternity, from the already existing Convention Fund, he divided among
the four western Psi Upsilon Chapters (Epsilon, Theta Theta, Zeta Zeta and
Theta Epsilon), each chapter to receive 1130.50. In the event that any chap
ter eligible for an allotment fails to send a delegate to the convention, its
portion of the sum shall revert to the treasury.
On motions duly adopted, the report was accepted, and the resolutions were
separately voted.
The president introduced Frank E. Booth, Delta '11, and WiUiam McPherson,
IV, Phi '34, each of whom addressed the convention briefly. He also introduced
Robert I. Laggren, Xi '13, former member of the Executive Council, Harry T.
Logan, Epsilon Phi '07, and Eugene Vinet, Epsilon Phi '11, two of the oldest
representatives of the host chapter in attendance.
On motion duly adopted, the convention adjourned at 11:40 a.m. to recon
vene at 2:30 p.m., Wednesday, September 6, 1961.

The chairman of the Committee on New Business, Brother Howe, recom

RESOLVED: That this convention accepts the petition of the Alpha Chi

Patrick N. Mullane, Gamma '62, chairman of the Committee on Academic
Standing and Awards, made an interim report and proposed the following

RESOLVED: That the Recorder of this convention be instructed to send
a letter of commendation to the Theta Epsilon Chapter for having attained
the highest relative scholastic standing in Psi Upsilon for the academic year
ended June, 1960.
RESOLVED: That the convention award the permanent plaque and the
rotating cup for the academic year ended June, 1960, to the Zeta Zeta Chapter
for its high scholastic achievement.
RESOLVED: That the Rho Chapter be commended for the highest
scholastic improvement during the academic year ended June, 1960, and
that the convention award the plaque to the Rho Chapter for this achievement.
On motions duly adopted, the resolutions were separately voted.
Donald P. Shaffer, Chi '62, chairman of the Committee on Legacies, sub

RESOLVED: That the Convention of 1961 approves the report of the
Committee on Legacies as herewith submitted and orders its officers to see

THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 7, 1961
Brittany Room
Sheraton-Mt. Royal Hotel
Montreal, Quebec, Canada
The convention was called to order by President Burton at 9:38 a.m. The
recorder called the roll of the chapters and reported that 22 chapters were repre
sented by delegates and a quorum was present.
On motion duly adopted, the reading of the minutes of the previous session
was dispensed with.
On motion duly adopted, the convention recessed at 9 :42 a.m.
The convention was called to order by the president at 10:33 a.m. Brother
Mullane, chairman of the Committee on Academic Standing and Awards, sub
mitted the final report of his committee (see Appendix F, page 32) .
On motion duly adopted, the report of the committee was accepted.
The Committee on the Value of International Fraternities was called upon
to submit its report. Alan M. Schlesinger, Mu '63, submitted the following reso
lutions of his committee:
RESOLVED: That all of the chapters of Psi Upsilon review the fra
ternity's history and objectives to realize better the solaces of fine friendship
between fine men chosen by our tried and tested Constitutional method of
unanimous selectivity to assure the true enjoyment of brotherhood, not only
in our own chapters, but in all of our chapters ;
That, in selecting new brothers, aU chapters keep before them the high
sensitivity of brothers in other chapters, so that the fraternity's membership
can always be cherished by every member ;
That the legions of great friendships established at conventions and
through inter-chapter visits prepare the undergraduate brothers in the com
pletion of their three or four years of undergraduate training for a fuller
participation in Psi Upsilon friendships in business and later life, no matter
where they reside, nor from which chapter they come ;
That adherence to fine traditions mutually accepted will guide us
through life, not only to achieve for ourselves, but also to help inspire those
who follow us ;
That, through an International Fraternity of the dignity and status of
Psi Upsilon, members can also carry on great works of brotherhood as exem
plified by The Psi Upsilon Foundation, Inc., through which alumni members
from all chapters may join together to help younger brothers from all
chapters ;
Page Nine

That, to quote from the words of the famous William Jewett Tucker,
Zeta 1861, former president of Dartmouth: "We have no touch of provincial
ism, and we do not subscribe to snobbishness or exclusiveness;"
That we agree with the Cornell Trustees who in 1957 said: "The right
of free association is an essential of democracy. This is the basis of strength,
as shown through fraternities ...
;"
That, to witness here at this convention the great friendships of older
brothers from so many chapters working for and supporting our several
chapters in Canada and the United States, through our Executive Council,
Alumni Association and the Foundation, inspires us to a greater belief in the
opportunities afforded by our International Fraternity;
That the above sentiments be recorded upon the minutes of this conven
tion and he subscribed to by all brothers here at this convention from Canada
and the United States.
On motion duly adopted, the report was accepted, and the resolutions were voted.
M. Roberts Hunt, Beta Beta '62, chairman of Rushing Committee A (smaller
colleges) submitted the committee's report. Because of the nature of the com
mittee. Brother Hunt stated that it had no resolutions to propose, but it made
the following recommendations: (1) that the chapter should take a strong stand
against the 100% opportunity system wherever and whenever possible; (2) that,
because of the relatively small active brotherhood (average 37 members), the
entire brotherhood should be required to attend all rushing meetings. On motion
duly adopted, the report of the committee was accepted.
Robert F. Bennett, Rho '62, chairman of Rushing Committee B (larger
universities) submitted the committee's report and proposed the following
resolutions :
RESOLVED: That the rushing chairman of each chapter prepare a brief
resume of its chapter's procedures, said resume to he circulated to every
chapter, no later than April 1, 1962, in the hope that all may profit from this
exchange of information.
RESOLVED: That a copy of this resolution he submitted to the Execu
tive Council and held for consideration by rushing committees at succeeding
conventions.
RESOLVED: That, in view of the importance of the subject of rushing.
Rushing Committees A and B, now regarded as Special Committees, be here
after recognized as Standing Committees, to be used as a vehicle for the
continuing exchange of vital information on the subject of rushing.
On motion duly adopted, the report was accepted, and the above resolutions were
voted.
Brother Howe, chairman of the Committee on New Business, led a discussion
relative to the desirability of Psi Upsilon joining the National Interfratemity
Council. The following resolution was proposed by Brother Joss :
RESOLVED: That the delegates of the 1961 International Psi Upsilon
Convention request the representation of Psi Upsilon on the National Inter
fratemity Council, such representation to begin immediately after the
convention.
On motion duly seconded, the resolution was defeated, 17 NAYS, 7 YEAS,
6 ABSENT.

following resolution:
RESOLVED: That the president of the Executive Council shall appoint
a committee of four undergraduates and two alumni for the purpose of in
vestigating the advisability of Psi Upsilon Fraternity joining the National
Interfratemity Council, said committee to report to the next convention on
its findings.
On motion duly adopted, the resolution was passed, 24 YEAS, 6 ABSENT.
(The president later appointed a committee comprised of the following under
graduates: Christopher Wiedenmayer, Zeta '63, Brian King, Delta Delta '63, dele
gate to the 1962 convention from the Epsilon Phi Chapter, Jonathan T. Howe,

T. Richards, Sigma '27, and Robert W. Parsons, Xi '22. If any of the undergradu

At the request of the president, John F. Bush, Jr., Upsilon '22, member of

recorder called the roll of the chapters and reported that 29 chapters were repre

On motion duly adopted, the reading of the minutes of the preceding session

Brother Howe, chairman of the Committee on New Business, continued the

RESOLVED: That the convention approve the use of a so-called "sweet
heart" fraternity pin of a smaUer size than the regular badge, the exact size

convention. He stated that the Omicron Chapter desired to hold the convention
in Champaign-Urbana, Illinois, in 1963 and invited the fraternity to accept the
Omicron's invitation.
Frank E. Booth, Delta '11, requested and received permission to address the
convention. He stated that the Delta was already making plans for the 1962
convention and looked forward to welcoming the delegates at that time.
Robert F. Bennett, Rho '62, was called upon by the president to explain
what steps the chapter took to improve its academic standing. He stated that the
Rho had instituted study halls for members who were not doing weU and generally
had expended more effort than in the past on academic pursuits.
A discussion of the absence of the Theta Epsilon Chapter was held. The
following resolution was proposed:
RESOLVED: That Stuart A. Clarke, Theta Epsilon '51, be caUed upon
to help revive the Theta Epsilon Chapter immediately.
On motion duly adopted, the resolution was voted.
Roland B. Winsor, Epsilon Phi '27, requested and received permission to
address the convention. He stated that the matter of "sweetheart" pins had not
been resolved and proposed the foUowing resolution:
RESOLVED: That a committee be appointed by the Executive Council
to investigate the recommendation of a "sweetheart" pin, or a change in the
Constitution of the fratemity relative to the wearing of the badge.
On motion duly adopted, the resolution was voted.
Edward T. Richards, Sigma '27, Vice President of The Psi Upsilon Founda
tion, Incorporated, discussed the Foundation and expressed the hope than an in
crease in its principal would enable it to make larger awards to undergraduates
in the future.
At the request of the chairman Brother Bush read the poem "Spring" written
by Richard Hovey, Zeta '85, for the convention of 1886.
James R. Sweet, Upsilon '62, chairman of the Committee to Foster, Protect
and Improve Ritual and Tradition, recommended that each chapter provide a
locked area for its Archives, chapter records, fraternity regalia and aU other mate
rial sacred to the chapter and the fraternity. In addition it was recommended that
the delegates famiUarize themselves with the correct Psi Upsilon handshake and
that, during the singing of the Shrine Song, hands be held at shoulder level dur
ing the verses to form the "Psi" and then raised on high during the chorus to
form the "Upsilon."
On behalf of his committee he made the following resolutions:

RESOLVED: That all pledges be required to learn the Shrine Song in
Its entirety.
1 J^^^P^^ED: That each chapter be aware that each meeting should in
clude a literary exercise, as stated in the Constitution, Article IV, Section 2,
which reads:
Each chapter shall hold not less than three meetings of a literary
character during each collegiate term.
^^^^^^^D: That the Executive Council appropriate an amount not to
exceed 1300 to record or restore and make available for purchase the six

RESOLVED: That the Psi Upsilon badge be worn verticaUy, over the

On motions duly adopted, the report of the committee was accepted, and the above

After affording an opportunity for further business, the president thanked
the delegates for their courtesy and interest in the proceedings and for their
attendance. He requested that the delegates report the proceedings of the con
vention to their chapters.
The president announced that, following the adjournment of the convention,
the Committee to Foster, Protect and Improve Ritual and Tradition would present
a formal meeting ceremony.
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn sine die was duly
adopted at 5:01 p.m.
RespectfuUy submitted,
Jerome W. Brush, Jr., Delta Delta '39

Appendix A
PSI UPSILON CONVENTION RULES
(As adopted April 7, 1892, and as amended by the Conventions of 1909,
1933, 1949, 1951 and 1959)
I
The delegate of the Executive CouncU, or, in the absence of such a delegate,
one of the delegates of the Chapter with which the Convention is held, shall
call the Convention to order and shaU appoint a Temporary President and a
Temporary Recorder.
H
The Temporary President shaU appoint two Committees of three or more
members each, as foUows:
1. A Committee on Credentials.
2. A Committee on Permanent Organization.
HI
The permanent officers shaU be a President, three or more Vice-Presidents, a
Recorder, and two Assistant Recorders.
IV
The Recorder and his Assistants shall record the proceedings of the Con
vention, and within twenty-four hours after the final adjournment shall transmit
to the Executive Council the record and aU papers relating to the business of
the Convention.
V
When the permanent officers shaU have been chosen, the Annual Com
munication of the Executive Council shall be read. The President shall then
appoint standing committees of four or more members each, as follows:
1. The Committee to Nominate Members of the Executive Council.
2. The Committee on Annual Communications and Unfinished Business,
which shall consider and report upon the matters embraced in the Annual Com
munication and the Treasurer's Report, as well as all measures considered, but
